hook.text: 'Going to' once meant walking toward something. Now it just means the future: 'gonna rain.'

buildup.text: Grammaticalization turns content words into grammar words—a one-way street of abstraction.

discovery.text: The French negative 'pas' was originally the noun 'step'—'I don't walk a step' became 'I don't.'

twist.text: The process is so universal that unrelated languages often grammaticalize the same words the same way.

climax.text: Body parts become prepositions, verbs become auxiliaries, nouns become suffixes—predictably.
